hypothesis: A 1m perp bar with an extreme return AND a volume spike marks forced liquidations, which overshoot; fading it at the next bar's open beats side-matched random twins over the following 6 hours.
mechanism: Liquidation engines market-sell (buy) leveraged positions regardless of price; the forced flow exhausts the book and price mean-reverts once it stops (liquidity-provision premium after forced selling).
closed_ideas_check: Nearest closed: research_loop shock_fade (ES 5m same-slot-scaled shocks, news-filtered) and its reverse, FAIL. F7 differs in market (crypto perps, 24/7, liquidation engines), bar (1m) and conditioning (volume spike >= 5x trailing median as the liquidation marker); the no-spike control below separates it from a generic shock fade. K-series crypto ideas (premium, OI, taker flow, DVOL) are different signals.

rules.ret: r_i = ln(c_i / c_{i-1}) on 1m closes; NaN when bar i-1 is not exactly 60 s earlier or either bar is stale.
rules.scale: sd_i = sample sd of r over the 1,440 bars BEFORE i (all 1,440 valid, else no signal); medv_i = median volume over the same 1,440 bars (> 0).
rules.signal: |r_i| >= k * sd_i AND v_i >= 5 * medv_i -> side = -sign(r_i), decided at bar i's close.
rules.exit: time exit 6h after entry; one open trade per symbol (engine run_book skips signals while a trade is open).

count_check: Before the run, count signals per asset (signals only, count-only train look); a config under 200 on BTC or ETH is dropped, not replaced (F4/F5/F6 precedent). Signals, not taken trades, are counted: overlapping signals inside an open trade reduce trades further, so a config with < 200 taken trades still fails on count in the run.
expected_sign: positive mean net R on BTC and ETH; not weaker at k = 10 than at k = 6.
against_the_mechanism: Report only (not gated, not in budget): the same rule with vol_mode='no_spike' (|r| >= k*sd but v < 5*medv). If no-spike fades do as well (mean net R >= the spike version on both assets), the volume spike (liquidation marker) adds nothing.
